CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit to evaluate the management of generalized anxiety disorder, insomnia, persistent fatigue, and tension-type headaches.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. John Smith returns for his follow-up appointment, reporting a moderate overall improvement in his symptoms since the last visit. He notes that his tension-type headaches have decreased in frequency to approximately once per week, with an average intensity of 2 out of 10. He attributes this positive change to the ongoing use of topiramate and amitriptyline, which he continues to take nightly without significant side effects.
Sleep quality has further improved, with Mr. Smith now averaging about 7 to 8 hours of sleep per night. He reports fewer awakenings and an easier time initiating sleep, particularly since the addition of low-dose gabapentin at bedtime, which he states has been beneficial. However, he still experiences occasional sleep disturbances related to work stress, prompting him to explore additional relaxation techniques.
Persistent fatigue remains a concern, especially in the mornings; however, Mr. Smith has noted a slight increase in energy levels throughout the day due to his consistent exercise routine, which includes running and yoga. He denies any new symptoms such as dizziness, lethargy, or changes in appetite.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder - diagnosed in 2021 2. Insomnia - diagnosed in 2021 3. Tension-Type Headaches - diagnosed in 2021 4. Hypertension - diagnosed in 2020, currently well-controlled on lisinopril 10 mg daily
MEDICATIONS
1. Sertraline 250 mg daily (continued) 2. Trazodone 50 mg at bedtime (continued) 3. Melatonin 10 mg at bedtime (continued) 4. Lisinopril 10 mg daily (continued) 5. Ibuprofen 400 mg as needed for headache relief (continued) 6. Amitriptyline 50 mg nightly (continued) 7. Topiramate 100 mg daily (continued) 8. Lorazepam 1 mg as needed (continued) 9. Gabapentin 100 mg at bedtime (newly added)
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Mr. Smith continues to work as a software engineer, where he has maintained effective time management strategies to reduce work-related stress. He remains physically active, participating in running and yoga, which he believes significantly enhance his mood and energy. His diet remains balanced, and he continues to abstain from alcohol while keeping his caffeine intake low.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
- Psychiatric: Anxiety levels stable; improved sleep quality; no suicidal ideation or depressive symptoms reported. - Neurological: Decreased headache frequency; no dizziness or visual disturbances reported. - Cardiovascular: No chest pain, palpitations, or dyspnea. - General: Mild fatigue persists, with no fever or weight changes.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
- Vital Signs: BP 118/74 mmHg, HR 68 bpm, RR 16 breaths/min, Temp 98.7F - General: Alert, oriented, appears well-groomed; mood appears stable with mild anxiety noted. - Neurological: Cranial nerves II-XII intact; no motor or sensory deficits observed; no dizziness reported. - Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm; no murmurs or gallops. - Psychiatric: Cooperative; maintains good eye contact; mood appears stable with no signs of distress.
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder: Continue sertraline at 250 mg daily. Monitor for any changes in anxiety levels. Lorazepam usage remains as needed for acute episodes. 2. Insomnia: Continue trazodone and melatonin; gabapentin at bedtime appears effective; monitor for any adverse effects or further sleep disturbances. 3. Tension-Type Headaches: Continue topiramate at 100 mg daily; monitor headache frequency and intensity. Continue amitriptyline at 50 mg nightly. Schedule a follow-up in one month to assess response to current regimen. 4. Persistent Fatigue: Reinforce the importance of regular physical activity and mindfulness practices. If fatigue persists or worsens, consider further evaluation for underlying causes.
Follow-up appointment is scheduled for 2029-07-01 to monitor symptom changes, evaluate treatment efficacy, and discuss any new concerns. Mr. Smith is encouraged to maintain a headache diary and track sleep patterns to identify potential triggers and improve management strategies.
